business_problem: Xiaoxun needed a more economical and stable cloud foundation for fast-growing child-watch services while also adding AI features that could increase user stickiness and make the devices more useful.
solution_summary: Xiaoxun and Baidu AI Cloud carried out a full cloud migration and service redesign for the company's child-watch business. At the infrastructure layer, Baidu mapped Xiaoxun's workloads onto a cloud architecture that could scale, stay stable and reduce operating cost at the same time. That environment supports the watch platform's communication, video and service functions while allowing resources to expand or shrink as demand changes. On top of infrastructure, Baidu supplied media-cloud capabilities for video encoding, distribution and playback so calls and video experiences became smoother and more reliable for end users. The final layer brought AI into the device experience: image recognition, scene recognition and speech recognition help children identify objects, ask daily questions, hear stories, play music and consume encyclopedia-style content from the watch itself. The result is a three-part architecture—core cloud migration, media-cloud delivery and embedded AI functions—that improves both platform economics and product differentiation.

data_flow: Watch-service traffic runs on the cloud platform and media stack, while user voice and visual inputs flow into the recognition services and return child-friendly answers, stories and learning content back to the wearable device.
business_outcome: Xiaoxun reduced cloud cost, improved service stability and used embedded AI features to make its watches more engaging and differentiated for families.
metrics: The AI platform's daily call volume increased by more than 30%.
